Alex G: Hey team — quick question. I'm demoing a prototype tomorrow and when I ran a small spike test I started getting a lot of 429s from the hosted API. Which key should I use for demos, and who do I ask for a short-term quota/burst?

Jamie (DevEx): Use the sandbox key for dev/demo load tests whenever possible. Hosted keys are reserved for production traffic. If you need a hosted burst for a live demo we can request a temporary increase.

Sam (Infra): To request a bump, open a support ticket in the Console (Help → Support → Request quota increase) and tag @infra. Provide: project id, expected peak QPS, duration window, and call pattern (streaming vs non-streaming).

Alex G: Thanks — side Q: does sandbox support streaming + embeddings? I saw 429s even on sandbox when I ran a small local generator.

Jamie (DevEx): Sandbox does support streaming and embeddings but has much smaller token and concurrent request buckets. For sustained load use a Dedicated or ask for a temporary hosted burst. For quick dev loops try reducing concurrency and using smaller batch sizes.

Linda (Eng): Also check whether your requests are hitting our proxy limits (corp VPN/CI runners sometimes share an IP). Quick check: run a curl from your laptop outside VPN and compare results:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SANDBOX_KEY" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-small","input":"hello"}'
```

Alex G: Good point — I was running the load from our CI. If it's an IP bucket issue, who can rotate the proxy or give a dedicated IP?

Sam (Infra): For demos we can sometimes provision a temporary egress IP for a short window — include that ask in the support ticket. If that's not possible, run the demo from a laptop or a cloud instance so you get a distinct IP.

Alex G: Any recommended retry/backoff strategy? My naive retries made the spikes worse.

Sam (Infra): Use exponential backoff with jitter; our SDKs implement this by default. See https://console.redwood.ai/docs/retries. Avoid tight synchronous retries and cap concurrent streams.

Jamie (DevEx): If you want, paste the support ticket link here and I'll follow up with infra during business hours. For tomorrow's demo we can usually turn around a temporary increase within 1–2 hours if capacity exists.

infra-bot: Support ticket #3456 created by Alex G — status: pending.

Alex G: Perfect — ticket is #3456, I switched my local tests to sandbox and throttled the loader. Will ping if anything changes. Thanks everyone! :thumbsup:
